Invalid values of sizes, insets and margins were only printed with
`console.warn`, e.g. for the `min-width:full;max-width:full` of the
buttons of vercel.com:

```
Invalid value "full" for "maxWidth". Expected a number or a percentage value (e.g., "50%").
```

With `onStyleError`, they're now reported to it like other invalid
values, instead of being printed. So stylesheets drop these declarations
like browsers, and an earlier valid one applies: with `.a { max-width:
30px } .b { max-width: full }`, an element with both classes is 30px
wide, as in Chrome. Before, the invalid one replaced it. Margins now
name their property in the message too.

`min-width: auto` and `min-height: auto`, the initial minimums, are
valid and leave the minimum unset, and `auto` of sizes and margins is
accepted in any case, like other keywords. Both were warnings before,
and would otherwise have been dropped from stylesheets.

Without `onStyleError`, they're still warnings rather than errors, so
renders that worked keep working.

The new tests check the reported errors of `width`, `minWidth`,
`maxWidth`, `top` and `marginLeft`, that nothing is printed, the
stylesheet case with the width Chrome gives, and that `auto` minimums of
a stylesheet override earlier ones with the size Chrome gives, with
snapshots.
